h1: Order of Nondisclosure (Record Sealing) Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: When a case ended in deferred adjudication or a conviction, expunction is usually off the table — but an order of nondisclosure can still seal it from employers, landlords and background-check companies. Attorney Robert Navar files these petitions in the El Paso court that handled your case.
summary: An order of nondisclosure under Texas Government Code Chapter 411, Subchapter E-1 seals a criminal record from the public and from private background-check companies, so most employers and landlords cannot see it.
It does not hide the record from law enforcement, prosecutors, courts, or state licensing agencies such as the Texas Medical Board, TEA or the State Bar.

Common paths: completed deferred adjudication (§ 411.072 and § 411.0725), certain misdemeanor convictions (§ 411.073 and § 411.0735), and a first DWI (§ 411.0731 and § 411.0736). Waiting periods vary and some offenses are excluded.
We confirm eligibility against the current statute, then quote a flat fee after a free consultation. Not sure whether you need this or an expunction? Call 915-503-1600.

sections.heading: What an Order of Nondisclosure Seals — and What It Doesn't
paragraphs: A nondisclosure order tells the court clerk, DPS and the arresting agencies that they may not release the record to the public, and DPS notifies the private background-check vendors that buy its data. The practical effect: when a private employer, apartment complex or volunteer organization runs a check, the case does not appear, and you may generally deny its existence on applications — except to the agencies that still have access.

Those exceptions matter. Criminal justice agencies keep full access, and a sealed case can still be used for enhancement if you are charged again. A long list of state entities also still see it: licensing boards for nurses, teachers, lawyers, peace officers and security guards, the Texas Juvenile Justice Department, school districts, the Department of Family and Protective Services, and more. If you are applying to one of those, you must still disclose the case. For federal jobs, military enlistment and clearances, treat the record as visible.
This is why we always check whether an expunction is possible first. Expunction destroys the record outright; nondisclosure is the remedy for cases that cannot be expunged.

sections.heading: Types of Nondisclosure Under Government Code Chapter 411
paragraphs: Subchapter E-1 is not one rule but a set of sections, each covering a different way a case can end. Which section applies decides whether you file a petition at all, how long you wait, and what you must prove. Eligibility also depends on your entire criminal history — a later conviction for anything other than a fine-only traffic offense can disqualify you.

list.text: for many first-time, non-violent misdemeanors, the court is required to issue the order when it discharges and dismisses the case, after you pay a small fee — no separate petition.
for deferred adjudication cases that do not qualify for the automatic order. Misdemeanors are generally eligible on discharge, or after a two-year wait for certain offenses; felonies wait five years.
a first misdemeanor conviction with probation or a short jail term may be sealed after a waiting period, generally immediate to two years depending on the offense and sentence.

a first driving-while-intoxicated conviction may be sealed after a waiting period — shorter if an ignition interlock was used — unless there was a crash involving another person or a BAC of 0.15 or more.
family-violence findings, sex offenses requiring registration, murder, human trafficking, stalking, injury to a child or elderly person and similar offenses are never eligible.

sections.heading: Waiting Periods and Eligibility Checks
paragraphs: Waiting periods run from the date you were discharged from deferred adjudication or completed your sentence, not from the arrest date. For a Class C deferred that ended in a county court, nondisclosure is generally available immediately after discharge; for misdemeanor deferred adjudication, generally after discharge or a two-year wait for offenses in certain Penal Code chapters; for eligible misdemeanor convictions, after the waiting period the statute assigns to that sentence. During the waiting period you must not be convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for any new offense other than a fine-only traffic ticket.

Those "other than a traffic ticket" words are where many El Paso petitions fail. Fine-only traffic offenses are generally carved out, but a Class B driving while license invalid or a paid non-traffic Class C like public intoxication may not be. We pull your DPS record and every El Paso court's disposition, and we confirm eligibility against the current statute before filing — the Legislature amends this subchapter almost every session.

sections.heading: Filing a Nondisclosure Petition in El Paso County
paragraphs: Unlike an expunction, which goes to district court, a nondisclosure petition is filed in the court that handled the original case: one of the El Paso County Courts at Law or Criminal Courts at Law for a misdemeanor, a district court for a felony deferred adjudication, or the municipal or JP court for a Class C deferred. All of the county courts sit at the courthouse at 500 E. San Antonio Ave downtown.

We draft the petition, attach the judgment and discharge order, pay the filing fee, and give the prosecutor notice. The State may request a hearing, and the judge must find that sealing the record is in the best interest of justice. For a client who completed probation cleanly, that finding is routine; where something needs context — a failure-to-appear warrant that was later recalled, for example — we address it in the petition. Once signed, the clerk sends the order to DPS, which notifies the agencies and private vendors; allow a few weeks for commercial databases to update.

sections.heading: What Employers See After the Order
paragraphs: A private employer in El Paso running a standard pre-employment check will see nothing for the sealed case, and under state law you may deny the arrest and prosecution on that application. Apartment screenings, most volunteer checks and private trucking and warehouse employers along I-10 fall in the same category.

Government and licensed employers are different. If you are applying to Fort Bliss as a civilian, to CBP, to a hospital, to EPISD or Ysleta ISD, or for any state license, assume the agency can see the sealed record and answer accordingly — a sealed case disclosed honestly is far less damaging than one discovered after a denial.

Our fee is a flat amount quoted after a free consultation, with court costs disclosed separately. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case. Schedule an appointment or contact us and bring any paperwork from the original case. Se habla español.

faqs.q: Does an order of nondisclosure erase my record?
faqs.a: No. It seals the record from the public and private background-check companies, but law enforcement, courts, prosecutors and a list of state licensing and child-care agencies keep access. Expunction is the remedy that actually destroys records, and it is available only for certain outcomes such as dismissals and completed Class C deferrals.

faqs.q: I completed deferred adjudication in El Paso. Do I automatically get nondisclosure?
faqs.a: Possibly. For many first-time, non-violent misdemeanor deferred adjudications, § 411.072 requires the court to issue the order at discharge once a fee is paid. If the court did not do so, or your case does not fit that section, we file a petition under § 411.0725. We check the court file to see which applies.

faqs.q: How long do I have to wait to seal a misdemeanor conviction?
faqs.a: It depends on the section. Eligible misdemeanor deferred adjudications are generally available at discharge or after two years for certain offenses; eligible misdemeanor convictions have their own waiting periods, and a first DWI typically waits two to five years depending on interlock use and sentence. We confirm the current period before filing.

faqs.q: What offenses can never be sealed?
faqs.a: Cases with an affirmative family-violence finding, offenses requiring sex-offender registration, murder, capital murder, aggravated kidnapping, human trafficking, stalking, injury to a child or elderly person, and violations of protective orders are excluded. A first DWI with a BAC of 0.15 or higher is also excluded from the DWI sections.

faqs.q: Which court do I file in?
faqs.a: The court that handled the original case — a County Court at Law for a misdemeanor, a district court for a felony deferred, or the municipal or JP court for a Class C. For El Paso County cases that means the courthouse at 500 E. San Antonio Ave downtown, or the municipal court at 810 E. Overland Ave for City of El Paso tickets.

faqs.q: Can I just handle this myself with the state's form?
faqs.a: Texas publishes a petition form, and some people file it successfully. The problems arise with eligibility: the wrong section, a miscounted waiting period or an overlooked later conviction gets the petition denied and the filing fee spent. A free consultation tells you which kind of case yours is.
